quotes.text: MCP is an open standard that lets AI applications discover and call tools and data sources in a structured way. Think of it like a universal remote.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Simple definition of MCP with a memorable analogy.

quotes.text: Customizations and ISV extensions become automatically visible to the agent. You don't need to write special code to expose your custom fields or custom processes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights why the dynamic server matters for customized ERP environments.

quotes.text: The agent uses the security permissions of the user identity that's connected. So whatever role-based access controls you've set up in Dynamics 365 apply automatically.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the security model: agents inherit the user's existing permissions.

quotes.text: We're moving from systems of record to systems of action. Instead of storing information and waiting for humans to act on it, the ERP becomes a platform that AI agents use to execute business processes directly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the structural shift MCP brings to ERP.

quotes.text: Plan for human in the loop for high-risk actions like posting large financial transactions or changing supplier terms. Monitor agent behavior and keep audit trails.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete governance advice for agentic ERP.

takeaways: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server exposes finance and operations functions to AI agents through one governed interface, and the dynamic version lets agents work through forms, including customizations and ISV extensions.
The analytics MCP server on Business Performance Analytics needs only two tools, get dataset schema and execute DAX query, and combining it with the action server turns insights into ERP actions.
Agents inherit the connected user's Dynamics 365 security, but the preview has limits such as a 120-second timeout, so start with low-risk tasks and keep a human in the loop for high-risk actions.
hook: Connecting AI assistants to an ERP used to mean custom APIs, connectors and security workarounds. This Simply Explained episode is for Dynamics 365 users, IT pros and partners who want to understand how the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server and the analytics MCP server let agents read ERP data and act on it through natural language, and how to try it safely in Copilot Studio or VS Code.
